title: The System NaCl-CaCl2-H2O. 2. Densities for Ionic Strengths of 0.1-19.2 mol/kg at 298.15 and 308.15 K and at 0.1 MPa
authors: Charles S. Oakes, John M. Simonson, Robert J. Bodnar
experimental_method: Relative densities of NaCl-CaCl2-H2O solutions (and the binaries) measured with a Paar DMA60/602HP vibrating-tube densimeter, calibrated with water and 5.552 mol/kg NaCl(aq), at nominal 298 and 308 K, 0.1 MPa.
uncertainties_stated: Pt resistance thermometers accurate within 0.01 K; temperature deviations from 298.15 K (up to 0.09 K) cause errors in V_phi generally below 0.04 cm3/mol and in rho at most 129 ppm; most results within 0.05 cm3/mol of the fit, corresponding to a maximum density uncertainty of about 400 ppm; fits for I < 1.0 mol/kg deviate more (>0.10 cm3/mol).
quality_remarks: Measurements are not strictly isothermal: tube temperature ranged 298.15-298.24 K and 308.12-308.15 K; the printed T column gives the actual value per sample. Low-I samples have poorer precision. One 308 K V_phi (25.035) was excluded from the authors' fit. The PDF is this paper only (pages 304-309, 6 pdf pages). Header of the PDF reads NaCl-CaCl2-H2O part 2.
not_extracted_tables: Table II: fitting parameters of the Pitzer model (model parameters, derived)
